title: A profinite span is approximated by compatible finite quotient spans
statement:
Use the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S_1,S,S_2$ be compact Hausdorff totally disconnected spaces in the smaller universe, and let $f_r:S_r\to S$ for $r=1,2$ be continuous maps. Here compact means that every open cover has a finite subcover; Hausdorff means that distinct points have disjoint open neighbourhoods; totally disconnected means that every connected subset has at most one point. A finite clopen partition means a finite set of pairwise disjoint nonempty open and closed subsets whose union is the whole space; the partition of the empty space is empty. Let $I$ be the set of triples $i=(\alpha_{1,i},\gamma_i,\alpha_{2,i})$ of such partitions of $S_1,S,S_2$, respectively, such that each block of $\alpha_{r,i}$ is contained in $f_r^{-1}(c)$ for a block $c\in\gamma_i$. Order $I$ by simultaneous refinement, with $i\le j$ when the partitions at $j$ refine those at $i$. Let $A_{r,i}$ and $C_i$ be the finite sets of blocks of $\alpha_{r,i}$ and $\gamma_i$; let $g_{r,i}:A_{r,i}\to C_i$ send a block to the block containing its image. Give all these finite sets the discrete topology. Set $B_i=\{(a_1,a_2)\in A_{1,i}\times A_{2,i}:g_{1,i}(a_1)=g_{2,i}(a_2)\}$. Refinement induces maps $b_{ji}:B_j\to B_i$ for $i\le j$.

Let $P=\{(s_1,s_2)\in S_1\times S_2:f_1(s_1)=f_2(s_2)\}$ with the subspace topology, and let $p_i:P\to B_i$ send a pair to its two blocks. The space $P$ is compact Hausdorff and totally disconnected. The canonical map
$$P\longrightarrow\{(x_i)\in\prod_{i\in I}B_i:b_{ji}(x_j)=x_i\text{ for every }i\le j\},\qquad p\longmapsto(p_i(p))_i,$$
is a homeomorphism, where the set on the right has the subspace topology of the product of the finite discrete spaces $B_i$.

proof.text: The pullback P is the equalizer of the two continuous maps S_1×S_2⇉S induced by f_1 and f_2. Since S is Hausdorff, this equalizer is closed in the compact Hausdorff product S_1×S_2, hence P is compact and Hausdorff. A connected subset of P is connected in S_1×S_2 and its two coordinate projections have connected images in the totally disconnected spaces S_1 and S_2; both projections are therefore constant, so the subset has at most one point. Thus P is totally disconnected. This is the standard closed-subspace/product argument underlying Stacks Tag 08ZY.

proof.text: The set I is nonempty: use the one-block partition on each nonempty space and the empty partition on an empty space; these are compatible (a nonempty $S_r$ has nonempty image, so $S$ is then nonempty). Given two compatible triples, intersect the blocks in each of the three coordinates and discard empty intersections. The resulting finite clopen partitions refine both triples. If a source intersection block $a\cap a'$ is nonempty, with $a\subseteq f_r^{-1}(c)$ and $a'\subseteq f_r^{-1}(c')$, then $a\cap a'\subseteq f_r^{-1}(c\cap c')$ and $c\cap c'$ is nonempty, so compatibility is preserved. Hence I is directed, and all A_{r,i}, C_i and B_i are finite discrete spaces. For $i\le j$ each block at $j$ lies in a unique block at $i$, giving maps $A_{r,j}\to A_{r,i}$ and $C_j\to C_i$. They commute with the $g$: if $a'\subseteq a$ with $a'\in A_{r,j}$, $a\in A_{r,i}$, then the nonempty set $f_r(a')$ lies in both $g_{r,j}(a')$ and $g_{r,i}(a)$, so the block of $\gamma_i$ containing $g_{r,j}(a')$ is $g_{r,i}(a)$. Hence the product map sends $B_j$ into $B_i$; this is $b_{ji}$, and $b_{ki}=b_{ji}\circ b_{kj}$ for $i\le j\le k$.

proof.text: Each coordinate p_i is continuous because the inverse image of a block is the corresponding clopen subset of P. Therefore the canonical map into the product of the finite discrete B_i, and hence into its compatibility subspace, is continuous. The source P is compact by step 1 and the target compatibility subspace is Hausdorff as a subspace of a product of finite discrete Hausdorff spaces. A continuous bijection from compact to Hausdorff is a homeomorphism. This proves the asserted homeomorphism with the displayed subspace topology.
